text.title: Mobile UX Basics: Touch Design, Navigation, and Performance Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a handset touch breakpoint exists at all, then on how many platforms one spec must bind, then on whether the surface collects input — separating "read the platform HIG instead" from the full per-platform numbers table.

decision-tree.root-question: Does this surface actually render at a handset breakpoint on a touch device?

branch.when: tablet-and-up or desktop-only tooling; there is no handset breakpoint

conclusion.verdict: skip; thumb zones, target-size floors and soft-keyboard rules have nothing to bind

branch.when: fixed hardware with a known screen and a stylus or physical keys — kiosk, POS, in-vehicle

conclusion.verdict: skip; the input model is not a thumb on a handheld screen, so the reach and keyboard rules do not apply — use the hardware vendor's interaction guidelines

branch.when: a handset breakpoint on a touch device is in scope
branch.question: How many platforms does this one spec have to bind?

branch.when: a single-platform native app, where Apple HIG or Material binds directly

conclusion.verdict: skip; the cross-platform divergence table this artefact exists to produce would have one column — read the platform guidelines instead

branch.when: web, or two or more platforms sharing one spec
branch.question: Does the surface collect text or numeric input from the user?

branch.when: it has forms — sign-in, checkout, search, one-time codes, addresses

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology including the field table: inputmode plus an autocomplete token per field, computed font-size at least 16 px so iOS Safari does not autozoom, and never type=number for phone, card, OTP or postcode

branch.when: no input fields — a read-only, browse-only or gesture-only surface

conclusion.verdict: apply the reduced set; record the strictest applicable floor per platform as a number, compute the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception rather than asserting it, and place primary actions in the lower third

branch.when: the surface has forms but no field-level performance data exists at the mobile field p75

conclusion.verdict: apply, but block sign-off on the budget row; LCP, INP and CLS must be stated at the 75th percentile of the mobile field segment with the lab proxy and throttling profile named
